thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Auto-page fired for service=edge-proxy (TLS handshake failure rate > 5% over 1m) :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PD INCIDENT #PD12345 — Trigger: edge-proxy.tls.handshake.errors. Initial alert at 5781234567. Escalation policy: oncall-eng-nyc -> jordan_sre -> oncall-eng-eu.

oncall-eng-nyc: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs and checking dashboards.

alice.m: seeing customer reports in #support: intermittent 502/525 from EU and APAC. Investigating error samples.

bob_ops: quick metrics — TLS handshake failure spike started ~5781234540 and peaked ~5781234590. ~12% of requests in eu-west-1 failing.

sam_network: running quick checks: dig results: ```dig +short edge.service.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8``` -> `10.2.34.21` `10.2.34.22`

sam_network: from our EU POP however dns cache resolves to `100.64.11.3` (old edge pool) — TTL for record is 300s. Looks like partial propagation mismatch.

jordan_sre: getting server-side TLS logs: a bunch of SSL errors: `SSL_ERROR_RX_RECORD_TOO_LONG` and `SSL: certificate subjectAltName does not match 'edge.service.redwood.ai'` on ~20% of handshakes. That points to wrong cert being served from some edge nodes.

alice.m: combining signals — some clients hit old IPs which have a cert with SAN=internal-edge.redwood.local (bad), others hit new IPs with correct prod cert. So clients with cached DNS -> bad TLS, new lookups -> ok.

bob_ops: checked ALB target health for the bad pool: targets show healthy at TCP level but app health check returning 503 intermittently because TLS handshake fails before HTTP.

sam_network: tcpdump snippet from affected node: ```Client Hello -> Server Hello (cert chain: CN=internal-edge.redwood.local)```

jordan_sre: this looks like a cert rotation step that didn't pick up proper prod cert on the old pool. Combined with Route53 partial updates it's a nasty intersection.

oncall-eng-nyc: plan: 1) reduce LB weight for legacy pool (100.64.11.x) to 0 to drain traffic, 2) re-issue/rollback cert on affected nodes, 3) invalidate bad cert from edge cache. I'll coordinate sequence.

product-ops: customer impact: external API calls to hosted inference return handshake errors for ~12% of EU requests. No data loss but elevated error rate and user-visible failures. Notify critical customers?

alice.m: support already notified top 5 paying customers, asking for logs and timelines.

bob_ops: executing weight change: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:tg:eu-west-1:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30``` then ```aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:listener:... --default-actions ...``` (rolling weight shift in progress).

sam_network: submitted Route53 rollback change (TTL still 300s): change-batch to restore previous A set pointing all traffic to 10.2.34.21/22. Change ID Z3ABCXYZ, propagation started.

jordan_sre: triggering cert rollback on affected edge nodes: ```ansible-playbook playbooks/certs/rollback-edge.yml -i hosts/eu-pool --extra-vars "target_version=prod-cert-v2025-03"``` — started.

incident-bot: Reminder: If ack not updated within 3m, escalate to jordan_sre.

oncall-eng-nyc: weight shift completed, removing 100.64.11.x from rotation. Observing handshake error rate drop from 12% -> 1.2% over the next 90s.

bob_ops: Route53 rollback completed (change status: INSYNC). Some ISPs still hitting stale cache but global reduction in failures.

ajordan_sre: cert rollback finished on all nodes in eu pool. Verified cert subject: `CN=edge.service.redwood.ai` with correct SANs.

alice.m: support: initial customer reports resolved for those who retried. We're still seeing a small tail due to DNS caching. Estimated % impacted now ~0.8%.

product-ops: are there any errors in logs indicating client retries or aborted sessions we should surface to customers?

jordan_sre: pulling post-mit logs. We'll provide timeline. Root cause appears to be an automated cert deployment that targeted a mixed set of edge images; some older images served internal cert. Simultaneous DNS change exposed the mismatch to a subset of clients.

oncall-eng-nyc: next steps: 1) verify all edge certs are consistent (rolling check), 2) add pre-deploy validation to cert rollout to verify SANs on every node before switching DNS, 3) increase Route53 TTL gating (do not change A sets for 5m after cert ops), 4) add monitoring alert for cert SAN mismatch.

bob_ops: adding alert rule: `edge.tls.cert.san.mismatch > 0` to fire to oncall and auto-mute the PD escalation if mitigation started.

incident-bot: PD INCIDENT #PD12345 status updated -> RESOLVED at 5781234920. Resolution summary: traffic drained from legacy pool; Route53 rollback; cert rollback and node validation. Impact: transient TLS handshake failures affecting ~12% peak EU traffic, reduced to <1% after mitigation.

alice.m: filing a postmortem doc and will link customers once ready. Will include timeline, rollback commands, and follow-up action owners.

product-ops: thanks team — please keep the incident channel pinned to the doc once it's up. :thumbsup:

jordan_sre: leaving notes for follow-ups: owner=jordan_sre, due=+48h, task=add SAN pre-flight check in CI, owner2=sam_network, task=DNS change runbook + safety TTL, owner3=bob_ops, task=alert and runbook for weight drains.

oncall-eng-nyc: handing off to next-day oncall: @jordan_sre you're primary for postmortem/questions. I'm dropping from channel.

incident-bot: auto-close reminder set for 72h.

product-ops: final customer comm draft will be reviewed tomorrow AM.

jordan_sre: end of thread — saving logs and timeline to /incidents/PD12345/logs and starting postmortem template.
